summary: Brief for THE SHAPE AND ITS SHADOW: a 170-second, seven-act silent mathematical film, distinguishing exact 3D geometry from the manuscript’s claimed all-dimensional result.
content:
Learner: a mathematically curious undergraduate familiar with coordinates, vectors and elementary volume, but new to convex duality and complex analysis.

Central question: how does a body constrain its polar, why does their volume product survive linear deformation, and how does the manuscript connect an analytic estimate to a geometric lower bound?

Prerequisite graph: coordinates → dot products → supporting half-spaces → polarity; tetrahedron volume → dissection → volume product; determinants → reciprocal volume scaling; convex hulls + signed constraint vectors → feasible simplices → integrated volume. Complex analysis enters as an explicitly attributed input, not an assumed prerequisite.

Teaching goals: derive the cube’s polar; compute its exact volume product; explain inverse-transpose invariance and the ball comparison; interpret every term of the manuscript’s inequality chain; recognize Hanner recursion while separating examples, proof architecture and unverified source claims.

Seven connected acts, totaling 170 seconds:

1. Constraint before name, 0–27s. Open with the title and coral cube K=[−1,1]^3. A normal vector y controls the plane x·y=1; show admissibility as every cube point satisfying x·y≤1. Boundary choices give supporting planes. Maximize over cube vertices to obtain |y₁|+|y₂|+|y₃|≤1, revealing the cyan octahedron. Only then name the polar K° and define its universal constraint. Explain that “shadow” is a title metaphor, not an optical projection.

2. Eight pieces, 27–49s. Establish cube volume 2³=8. Separate the eight exact tetrahedra conv(0,s₁e₁,s₂e₂,s₃e₃), sᵢ∈{−1,1}. Focus on one: triangular base area 1/2, perpendicular height 1, volume (1/3)(1/2)(1)=1/6. Reassemble: |K°|=8/6=4/3; P(K)=32/3=4³/3!.

3. Reciprocal motion, 49–68s. Continuously stretch by positive diagonal T toward diag(2,3/2,1/2); update the polar using T⁻ᵀ at every instant. Explain transpose-inverse, determinant and reciprocal scaling. Volumes become 12 and 8/9; their product stays 32/3.

4. A round comparison, 68–82s. Transition to the unit ball. Explain self-polarity using x·y≤‖x‖‖y‖ and equality along matching directions. Display volume 4π/3, then product 16π²/9≈17.546>10.667.

5. The analytic lens, 82–106s. Define a convex body as compact, convex, with nonempty interior; require origin symmetry K=−K. Attribute the all-dimensional bound P(K)≥4ⁿ/n! to the manuscript; note that the symmetric 3D result predates it. On a tilted plane, show D={v+it: |t|≤1, |v|≤λ(t)}, explaining real coordinate, imaginary coordinate and width. Label the drawing “schematic of the analytic input.” Identify boundary sampling and the holomorphic mass estimate as the source of S≥1, without simulating a proof.

6. From feasibility to volume, 106–150s. Define A by |bᵢ·X|≤1 and A°=conv{±bᵢ}. Explain L_X as the constraints |bᵢ·Y|≤λ(bᵢ·X). A signed basis is feasible when its unique tight-constraint solution lies in L_X; Σ_X collects its simplices. Build only the exact cube-example tetrahedra. All eight orthants tile its polar for every interior X; general bodies can leave gaps. Reveal sequentially 1≤S=Σ_I P_I=(n!/4ⁿ)∫_A|Σ_X|dX≤(n!/4ⁿ)|A||A°|. Define I, feasibility probability P_I, dimension n, factorial, volume and integration over X. Link the equality to boundary sampling/change of variables and the final inequality to containment. State approximation extends the polytope result.

7. Equality’s family, 150–170s. Build Hanner examples recursively from centered intervals using Cartesian products and conv((H₁,0)∪(0,H₂)); show polarity exchanging these operations. Attribute equality precisely to invertible linear images of Hanner bodies. Explain that classification needs a separate argument. Close with the required dated family-087 source card and formalization caveat.

Acceptance: actual runtime 150–180s; one self-contained Manim CE 0.19 Cairo ThreeDScene, CPU-oriented, without runtime network, external assets, custom file IO or SciPy. Every mathematical scene uses genuine depth, restrained meshes, parallax, world-space LaTeX, deliberate camera flights and term zooms. Captions replace one another; at most one explanatory caption and one active formula group dominate. Hold dense explanations with a settled camera; audit clipping, occlusion and readability throughout motion. Require independent Astra mathematical and rendered-motion audits. Jev remains off; no approval claim.
checks: Python exact arithmetic confirmed tetrahedron volume 1/6, octahedron volume 4/3 and product 32/3; numerical calculation confirmed the ball product 17.5459633797 and reciprocal stretch volumes 12 and 8/9.

Fetched family 087 documentation at the pinned revision; it reports the symmetric inequality and Hanner equality classification. Lean was not run; the PDF proof was not independently checked in this brief.
Manim imports failed in both the default Python and repository virtual environment. Local API inspection and render verification remain uncompleted; no compatibility or visual-success claim is made.
No files edited, repository changes made, agents delegated or Jev reviews invoked.
